rationale: This observational cross-sectional study (household survey of n=280 across two semi-arid Rajasthan cities plus NSSO 69th round descriptive statistics, analyzed via chi-square tests and binary logistic regression) examines socio-economic and spatial-institutional determinants of drinking water supply along the urban-rural continuum (city core, outer municipal wards, peri-urban village under Gram Panchayat, and rural village). Among rule/governance dimensions, the central mechanism is institutional_structure_coordination: the urban-rural jurisdictional dichotomy leaves outer fringes and peri-urban villages caught between municipal water governance and rural Gram Panchayat arrangements without institutional piped coverage (with monthly water payment explicitly interpreted by the authors as a proxy for municipal supply vs reliance on informal private tankers rather than a tariff-rule exposure; confidence is medium given the heavy co-emphasis on socio-demographic predictors). For outcomes, the binary dependent variable ('good drinking water supply') co-equally combines physical piped connection within premises (primary_connection) with daily supply continuity, sufficiency, exclusive accessibility, and defect-free water quality (effective_access), warranting effective_access as primary_outcome_family and multiple for assigned_outcome_label_with_multiple.
